description: We are a passionate team interested in space exploration, artificial intelligence, and engineering. Our project focuses on improving astronaut safety by studying fire behavior in microgravity and developing innovative early-warning solutions. We aim to combine NASA research data, AI, and Arduino technology to explore fire risks in space. We welcome motivated members with skills in programming, AI, electronics, data analysis, and research.
summary:
AstroShield – Smart Fire Detection and Safety System for Spacecraft

AstroShield is an innovative fire safety project developed by our team, Bahrain Astronauts, to improve astronaut safety during space missions.

Fire is especially dangerous in space because flames, smoke, and gases behave differently in microgravity, making early detection and emergency response more challenging.

Our project introduces a smart fire detection and warning system using an Arduino microcontroller, an MQ-2 gas and smoke sensor, LED indicators, and a buzzer. The system continuously monitors the surrounding environment. When smoke or dangerous gas levels exceed a set threshold, it is designed to activate a red warning light and an audible alarm. Under normal conditions, a green LED indicates a safe environment.

AstroShield also proposes future integration with AI-powered analysis of NASA’s microgravity combustion research to improve fire detection and support safer emergency responses.

Our goal is to develop an affordable, practical, and expandable safety solution that contributes to protecting astronauts and supporting future space exploration.
details:
AstroShield is a smart fire detection and warning system developed by our team, Bahrain Astronauts, to explore ways of improving fire safety during space missions.

Our project uses an Arduino UNO, an MQ-2 gas and smoke sensor, LED lights, and a buzzer to detect potential hazards and provide early warnings. When gas or smoke levels exceed a programmed threshold, the system is designed to activate a red warning light and buzzer. Under normal conditions, a green light indicates safety.

AstroShield is inspired by NASA’s research on combustion in microgravity, where fire behaves differently than on Earth. Our future goal is to integrate artificial intelligence with NASA’s combustion datasets to analyze experimental results, identify patterns, and provide useful fire safety insights through an interactive dashboard.

This project is important because fire presents a serious risk during space missions. By combining an affordable physical prototype with future AI-powered research, AstroShield aims to contribute to safer environments for astronauts exploring the Moon, Mars, and beyond.
